machine: Apple M1 Max, 32 GB unified memory, macOS 26.6.2
scope: Integrated cost of each part of one cached 1024 transformer step (4,096 target rows plus a 31-row cached prefix), measured by omitting that work from all 32 blocks with QI_PROFILE_SKIP and subtracting step-2 wall time from adjacent full runs
method_caveat: Ablation measures what the step loses when a part is absent, including overlap effects; skipped runs produce meaningless output. GPU utilization was 5-32% from desktop activity before the first series, and a steady 5% before the second.

series_2.proj: Run aborted non-finite: the stale projected buffer later feeds padded K/V. Its cost is inferred as MLP minus gate minus down.

breakdown.part: all other kernels (norms, RoPE, SwiGLU, residuals, K/V preparation)

peak_assumption: 10.6 TFLOP/s FP16/FP32 for the 32-core M1 Max GPU

rejected_split_gemm.idea: Encode each 12288-wide or 12288-deep MPS GEMM as three 4096-wide slices (deep slices accumulate with beta 1), hoping each slice would match the 88% attention-output shape
rejected_split_gemm.result: 8.81 s versus 8.72 s mean, within the 0.12 s spread between identical current-path runs. Slices run at the same efficiency as the whole GEMM, so the shortfall is inside MPS kernel selection rather than the call shape. The prototype was removed.

conclusion: Attention is the least efficient part (62% of peak) but only 15% of the step; MLP GEMMs are 55% at 76%, but reshaping MPS calls does not recover the gap. Expected exact-arithmetic opportunity per 13-full-step Cache-DiT image: about 5 s from attention at 85% of peak.
